seo.title: How to Get on Best-Of Lists That AI Search Cites
seo.meta_description: How to get on best-of lists that AI tools cite: why roundups shape AI recommendations, which lists matter, honest ways to be included, and what to avoid.

h1: How to Get on the Best-Of Lists That AI Answers Draw From
answer: Best of lists, such as "best GEO agencies" or "top CRM tools for small teams", shape AI recommendations because assistants often search for these roundups and summarize them. To be included honestly, identify the lists that rank for your category, make it easy for editors to evaluate you with clear facts and proof, earn reviews, and build relationships rather than paying for undisclosed placements.
key_takeaways: AI tools often draw on roundup articles for recommendation questions.
Find the lists that already appear for your category's queries.
Give editors facts, pricing and proof that make evaluation easy.
Reviews and directory ratings feed many lists.
Disclose any paid or sponsored placements.

sections.heading: Why best-of lists matter for AI
sections.body_html: When someone asks an assistant "what are the best GEO agencies in Orange County" or "which accounting software is best for freelancers", the AI often searches the web and reads articles that compare options. The brands that appear repeatedly across those roundups are the ones most likely to be named in the answer. Being absent from every list makes it harder for an AI to include you, however good your own website is.

sections.heading: Find the lists that matter
sections.body_html:
1. Search your category's "best" and "top" queries in Google and note the roundups on the first two pages.
  2. Ask ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini the same questions with web search on, and note which articles they cite.
  3. Check industry publications and directories that publish rankings or awards.
  4. Record who publishes each list, when it was last updated and how brands are chosen.

Prioritize lists that are cited by AI tools and updated regularly.

sections.heading: Understand how editors choose
sections.body_html: Editors of good roundups compare features, pricing, reviews, track record and fit for specific audiences. Many update lists periodically and accept suggestions. Some lists are based on directory ratings or review platforms. Others are affiliate or sponsored lists. Knowing the method tells you whether to focus on reviews, on outreach to the editor, or on a directory profile.

sections.heading: Make your brand easy to evaluate
sections.body_html:
• A clear one-line description of what you do and who you serve.
  • Transparent pricing or pricing ranges.
  • Specific differentiators, stated plainly.
  • Proof: client results shared with permission, case studies, certifications.
  • A press or media page with logos, screenshots and contact details.

Editors on a deadline include the options they can understand quickly and verify.

sections.heading: Reach out the right way
sections.body_html: When a relevant list is updated regularly, send the editor a short, specific note: what you offer, why it fits their audience and criteria, and where to verify the facts. Do not ask to be ranked first or demand changes. Offer a demo, trial or data that would help their evaluation. Many editors appreciate accurate information, especially when it helps their readers.

sections.heading: Reviews and directories feed lists
sections.body_html: Many roundups lean on ratings from review platforms and industry directories. Keep your profiles on the platforms relevant to your category complete and accurate, and ask satisfied clients to review you there. Steady, genuine reviews raise your chances of appearing on lists that filter by rating.

sections.heading: Paid placements and disclosure
sections.body_html: Some lists sell placements. If you pay for inclusion, make sure the placement is clearly disclosed as sponsored, as advertising rules in many places require. Undisclosed paid rankings can mislead readers, and a list known to be pay-to-play carries less weight with careful readers. Earned inclusion on credible lists is worth far more.

sections.heading: Create your own honest comparison
sections.body_html: Publishing a fair comparison of options in your category, including competitors, can itself become a source AI tools cite. Be balanced: explain who each option suits, including when a competitor is the better choice, and state your own bias clearly. A self-serving list that ranks yourself first on every criterion is less credible and less likely to be used.

sections.heading: Keep listings current
sections.body_html: Lists go out of date. Set a reminder to review the main roundups for your category each quarter, update editors when your offering changes significantly, and correct outdated information politely. Stale facts in a popular list can be repeated by AI tools long after they stop being true.

sections.heading: How to measure progress
sections.body_html: Track how many of the important roundups include you, referral traffic from them, and whether AI answers to "best" questions in your category start to name you. Note the reasons AI tools give when they mention you; they often echo the language used in the lists.

sections.heading: An example outreach note
sections.body_html: A short note to an editor might read: "Hi, I noticed your guide to GEO agencies in Southern California was updated in March. We are an Orange County agency focused on AI search visibility for local service businesses, with published pricing ranges and case studies at the links below. If you review the list again, we would be glad to provide a walkthrough or answer questions. Thanks for keeping the guide current." It is specific, useful and easy to say no to, which is why it works.

sections.heading: What to do if you are not included
sections.body_html: Do not argue with editors or ask for rankings to be changed. Instead, look at what the included options have that you lack: more reviews, clearer pricing, published results, a recognized award. Close those gaps, then let the editor know when something genuinely changes. Inclusion often follows naturally once the evidence is there.

faqs.q: Why do best-of lists matter for AI search?
faqs.a: Assistants often search for and summarize roundup articles when answering recommendation questions, so brands that appear across several credible lists are more likely to be named.

faqs.q: How do I find which lists AI tools use?
faqs.a: Ask ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini your category's best-of questions with web search on and note which articles they cite, alongside Google's top results.

faqs.q: How do I get added to a best-of list?
faqs.a: Make your brand easy to evaluate with clear facts and proof, build reviews, and send a short, specific note to editors of lists that are updated regularly.

faqs.q: Should I pay to be on a list?
faqs.a: Only if the placement is clearly disclosed as sponsored. Earned inclusion on credible lists is more valuable and more trustworthy.

faqs.q: Can I publish my own best-of list?
faqs.a: Yes, if it is honest and balanced, including competitors and saying who each option suits. A self-serving list is less credible.

faqs.q: Do reviews help me get on lists?
faqs.a: Yes. Many roundups use ratings from review platforms and directories, so steady, genuine reviews improve your chances.

faqs.q: How often should I check the lists?
faqs.a: Quarterly is a good rhythm. Update editors when your offering changes and correct outdated facts politely.

faqs.q: Do awards count as best-of lists for AI?
faqs.a: Credible industry awards and rankings can work in a similar way, because they are independent sources that describe your business positively and specifically.
